task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a reported feature of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about the municipal nursery preparing future street trees for the city of Bellmarsh. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Bellmarsh municipal nursery holds about 800 young trees at different stages of growth for future public planting.
The nursery's current planning list identifies about 200 as candidates for the next planting season, not 800 trees ready to leave immediately.
Nursery supervisor Hessa Dale walks the rows with a clipboard linking each batch to its origin, potting history and intended size range.
The supplied scene describes staff moving a batch to a new spacing so its branches and root containers have room as the trees grow.
A tree's presence at the nursery does not guarantee that it will be suitable for every proposed street location.
Dale said, "People see the planting day. We are working on the years that have to happen before that day is possible."
The planting team considers available space, overhead and underground services and expected maintenance when matching nursery stock to a site.
Some trees remain at the nursery for another season when their condition or the destination site's preparation is not ready.
The city also buys some stock from outside growers, so the municipal nursery is not the sole source of every public tree.
Neighborhood volunteer Rena Sore helps record street planting requests and visits the nursery to understand the choices available.
Sore said, "On the street we ask for a tree this winter. Here you can see how far back somebody had to begin."
The nursery's records distinguish stock held, stock allocated and trees actually planted.
An allocation can change if a planned street project is delayed, rather than require a tree to be planted at an unsuitable time or unfinished site.
Staff record trees that do not remain suitable for planting rather than count every seedling or purchased sapling as a future completed street tree.
The packet supplies no universal survival rate or forecast of carbon storage for the 800 trees.
The nursery occupies land beside a former parks depot and shares some storage and delivery access with the maintenance team.
The work includes watering, spacing, condition checks and updating records, not only planting seeds and waiting for them to grow.
The city has a current operating budget for the nursery, but future street-planting projects require their own site and maintenance allocations.
The supervisor keeps examples of older plant labels to explain how batch names have changed without losing the link to earlier records.
The nursery is not open for unrestricted public collection of trees; community planting requests go through the city's parks process.
A planned public visit will show the growing stages and record system rather than promise each visitor a tree to take home.
No citywide canopy-growth result or claim that every approved planting request can be met is included in the supplied record.

forbidden_additions: Eight hundred planting-ready trees or a guaranteed tree for every request.
A universal survival rate, measured carbon benefit or citywide canopy result.
Unrestricted public collection or a fully funded destination for every tree.
preserve: The long preparation period and the matching of growing stock to actual sites.
Stock, allocation and completed planting as different stages.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
